anti_patterns: Do not instantiate application services directly inside FastAPI endpoints.
Do not bypass typed dependency aliases from project/infrastructure/api/dependencies.py.
Do not read environment variables in business logic; use project.core.config.get_settings.
Do not create alternate service registries outside composition_root and service_registration.

checks: endpoint modules must not import application services directly
endpoint parameters must use typed dependency aliases for service injection
endpoint alias -> getter -> service_key chains must resolve through dependencies.py
endpoint modules must not instantiate services directly

guidance_only_rules.summary: The declared allowed dependencies are runtime_enforced as a whitelist gate: a domain module may import the standard library and project.domain, and nothing else.
Forbidden import prefixes are runtime_enforced. Declared allowed dependencies remain guidance_only and are not_enforced_in_validator as a whitelist gate.
Infrastructure keeps broad dependency freedom, but runtime assembly and entrypoint imports are runtime_enforced forbidden prefixes.

project/core/composition_root.py.classification_reason: Composition-root wiring is a reusable template surface and the canonical entrypoint for shared dependency assembly.
project/core/composition_root.py.role: Shared composition root for service construction and FastAPI app assembly.
project/core/composition_root.py.why_it_exists: Keeps shared runtime wiring in one canonical place so services are created once and exposed through app.state.services.

project/core/lifecycle.py.classification_reason: Lifecycle wiring is reusable kernel infrastructure — verticals consume it without modifying it.
project/core/lifecycle.py.role: FastAPI lifespan controller that opens shared async resources at startup and closes them at shutdown.
project/core/lifecycle.py.why_it_exists: Centralizes ordering of pool and LLM startup and teardown so heavy resources are created once and released cleanly when the application stops.

project/core/service_registration.py.classification_reason: Vertical registration is reusable template infrastructure that every derived Mayak project follows.
project/core/service_registration.py.role: Vertical-service wiring registry layered on top of the shared composition root.
project/core/service_registration.py.why_it_exists: Keeps feature-specific service construction out of the shared composition root while preserving one canonical registration flow.

project/infrastructure/agents/llm_servic.classification_reason: Shared LLM facade is reusable kernel infrastructure consumed by verticals through the composition root.
project/infrastructure/agents/llm_servic.role: LLM service facade composing live-provider, mock-mode, and readiness mixins.
project/infrastructure/agents/llm_servic.why_it_exists: Provides one canonical entry point for LLM calls so verticals depend on a stable facade and the live/mock split stays consistent.

project/infrastructure/api/dependencies..classification_reason: Endpoint dependency aliases are reusable wiring infrastructure and are enforced by runtime validators.
project/infrastructure/api/dependencies..role: Typed FastAPI dependency alias registry for endpoint-facing service access.
project/infrastructure/api/dependencies..why_it_exists: Provides the single canonical alias -> getter -> service_key surface that endpoints must use instead of importing or constructing services directly.

project/infrastructure/api/endpoints/hea.classification_reason: Canonical thin-endpoint reference shipped in the kernel; consumed by the add_endpoint task and surfaced via CANONICAL_EXAMPLES.thin_endpoint.
project/infrastructure/api/endpoints/hea.role: Sample readiness/liveness endpoint and canonical thin-endpoint reference.
project/infrastructure/api/endpoints/hea.why_it_exists: Demonstrates the readiness contract (services + LLM + db connectivity) and ships as the kernel's canonical reference for the add_endpoint task.

project/infrastructure/api/exception_han.classification_reason: Shared exception mapping is reusable kernel infrastructure consumed by every endpoint.
project/infrastructure/api/exception_han.role: Centralized FastAPI exception handlers mapping domain errors to typed HTTP responses.
project/infrastructure/api/exception_han.why_it_exists: Keeps error→status mapping in one place so endpoints stay thin and the failure surface stays uniform across verticals.

project/infrastructure/api/middleware.py.classification_reason: Shared HTTP middleware is reusable kernel infrastructure that runs for every request — wiring touches affect every endpoint.
project/infrastructure/api/middleware.py.role: AI-optimized HTTP middleware that opens semantic-logging spans and propagates trace context.
project/infrastructure/api/middleware.py.why_it_exists: Hooks every request into the semantic logger so spans, request IDs, and business-context headers are captured uniformly across verticals.

project/infrastructure/api/router_regist.classification_reason: Router registration is part of the reusable wiring kernel rather than sample business behavior.
project/infrastructure/api/router_regist.role: Canonical router inclusion surface for FastAPI endpoint modules.
project/infrastructure/api/router_regist.why_it_exists: Centralizes router ownership so new routes are registered predictably and can be discovered by validators and AI context generation.

pyproject.toml.classification_reason: Defines reproducible build/dev environment for every Mayak project. Changes ripple to lockfile, mypy gate, ruff gate, and coverage tooling.
pyproject.toml.role: Project-wide Python packaging, dependency, and tool configuration.
pyproject.toml.why_it_exists: Single source for runtime/dev dependencies, build backend, and tooling configs (ruff, mypy, coverage, pytest). Drives uv.lock and CI reproducibility.

scripts/doctor_ai_context.py.classification_reason: Doctor wires together every validator and is invoked by quality-gates on failure. Edits ripple into the entire failure-recovery loop.
scripts/doctor_ai_context.py.role: Diagnostic backbone that pinpoints the first blocking layer when quality-gates fails.
scripts/doctor_ai_context.py.why_it_exists: Provides actionable error narratives instead of raw validator output, extending coverage to all gates run by quality-gates and routing agents to the smallest fix recipe via failure_playbook.

scripts/generate_ai_context.py.classification_reason: This generator defines the reusable machine contract consumed by validators and query tooling.
scripts/generate_ai_context.py.role: Generator for machine-readable repository context and architecture contracts.
scripts/generate_ai_context.py.why_it_exists: Builds the JSON artifacts that back onboarding, query routing, and drift checks without introducing a separate documentation stack.

scripts/query_ai_context.py.classification_reason: The query CLI defines the reusable operating interface for the repository itself.
scripts/query_ai_context.py.role: Repo operating API for AI agents and narrow navigation workflows.
scripts/query_ai_context.py.why_it_exists: Exposes stable query commands so agents can inspect wiring, policy, failure remediation, and minimal context without broad repository scans.

scripts/validate_architecture.py.classification_reason: Architecture validation is part of the reusable enforcement kernel for derived repos.
scripts/validate_architecture.py.role: Runtime validator for forbidden layer imports and architecture rule enforcement.
scripts/validate_architecture.py.why_it_exists: Turns the most important layer boundaries into executable checks rather than leaving them as narrative guidance only.

scripts/validate_endpoint_wiring.py.classification_reason: Endpoint wiring validation is reusable enforcement infrastructure, not sample code.
scripts/validate_endpoint_wiring.py.role: Runtime validator for endpoint dependency-alias and wiring contracts.
scripts/validate_endpoint_wiring.py.why_it_exists: Guards the thin-endpoint pattern so routes stay on typed aliases instead of importing or constructing services directly.

scripts/validate_runtime_ownership.py.classification_reason: Runtime ownership validation is reusable enforcement infrastructure for the template.
scripts/validate_runtime_ownership.py.role: Runtime validator for shared-resource, environment access, and app.state ownership.
scripts/validate_runtime_ownership.py.why_it_exists: Turns resource ownership rules into executable checks so LLM edits cannot drift shared runtime wiring into endpoints or business logic.

application.enforcement_summary: Forbidden import prefixes are runtime_enforced. Declared allowed dependencies remain guidance_only and are not_enforced_in_validator as a whitelist gate.

narrative_notes: Declared allowed dependencies describe the intended layer contract.
They are guidance-only unless mirrored by runtime-enforced rules.

not_enforced_in_validator.explanation: Declared allowed dependencies describe the intended layer contract, but validate_architecture.py does not enforce them as a whitelist gate.

enforcement_notes: Runtime validation currently enforces forbidden import prefixes only.
Declared allowed dependencies remain architectural guidance, not a whitelist gate.

domain.enforcement_summary: The declared allowed dependencies are runtime_enforced as a whitelist gate: a domain module may import the standard library and project.domain, and nothing else.

narrative_notes: Declared allowed dependencies describe the intended layer contract.
They are guidance-only unless mirrored by runtime-enforced rules.

not_enforced_in_validator.explanation: The declared allowed dependencies ARE the whitelist gate for this layer: validate_architecture.py rejects any import outside them and the standard library.

enforcement_notes: Runtime validation enforces the allowlist, so a library nobody thought to ban is rejected by default.
The standard-library half comes from sys.stdlib_module_names and needs no maintenance.

infrastructure.enforcement_summary: Infrastructure keeps broad dependency freedom, but runtime assembly and entrypoint imports are runtime_enforced forbidden prefixes.

narrative_notes: Declared allowed dependencies describe the intended layer contract.
They are guidance-only unless mirrored by runtime-enforced rules.

not_enforced_in_validator.explanation: Declared allowed dependencies describe the intended layer contract, but validate_architecture.py does not enforce them as a whitelist gate.

enforcement_notes: Infrastructure may depend on project.core utility modules such as config and logging.
Runtime assembly modules and launcher entrypoints remain runtime_enforced forbidden imports.
